invariants.residual: The verdict is now CONSUMED, and what is left is narrower than the statement rather than absent from it. MDK persists the halt on the group, so the verdict needs no confirmation on this side: `LiveEventRouter._handleStatus` reads `unrecoverableNostrGroupId` BEFORE its null-reason early return, resolves the circle and refreshes it on the FIRST nudge (`_handleUnrecoverable`), keeping no per-circle state of its own. The refreshed circle reads `CircleEngineState.unrecoverable` from its row, and every surface follows that state rather than the event: the circle leaves the publish-eligible set (`filterPublishEligibleCircles`), Circle details offers it no member mutation, and its sharing card in Circle details names it (`sharingHealthTitleUnrecoverable`, `sharingHealthBodyUnrecoverable`) with a re-create that opens the create flow with this circle's display name pre-filled (`legacyCircleRecreateCta`) and touches the broken group not at all, so the cached roster and last-known locations stay readable beneath it. This entry still declares no `assertion_arb_keys`, and that is deliberate rather than leftover: its promise is that the wedge is DETECTED and NAMED per circle, not any particular sentence of copy; the card's copy is held by its own copy-accuracy tests. The verdict is the engine's own and terminal, and nothing on this device repairs the circle. One limit of the detection itself, argued at `report_unrecoverable_circles`: the verdict is evaluated only where a session is served as the foreground's — a foreground re-anchor, or the claim that promotes a started session — and never at `start`. On Android a return to the foreground is a fresh start and that claim, never a foreground open (the engine was stopped at the pause): the claim makes this report and asks for a drive of the stored records, which the session's drive task then makes, paced. Half (a)'s SUPPRESSION is scoped to the live-sync burst plane, and its supporting guarantee is tree-wide since W9q: a fanout is the only way a commit leaves the device, and only the driver rolls one back, on proof (`a_fanout_is_the_only_way_a_commit_leaves_the_device`). A commit no relay acknowledged stays recorded and is sent again by the next full drive; a background wake makes none. FINALLY, half (b) is LIVE-SYNC-SHAPED: `report_unrecoverable_circles` is invoked only where a live session is served as the foreground's, and the poll configuration (`HAVEN_LIVE_SYNC=false`) starts no session, so a circle it wedges gets no per-circle `GroupUnrecoverable` verdict; the flag-independent sharing-health banner still reports the silence, and a circle whose own decrypt returns `Unrecoverable` still reads `CircleEngineState.unrecoverable` at the circle list's next load on either plane, and its sharing card reads the core's `unrecoverable` recovery cause at its next derivation — an open owner question (`docs/POWER_EFFICIENCY_PLAN.md` §9.9). AN ADMIN'S OWN REMOVAL THIS DEVICE STAGED AND NEVER RESOLVED — a kill interrupted it — is restored at the next open under a fanout record (`try_recordless_removals`). A drive in the full mode resolves it. In the live-sync configuration that drive is asked for by the claim the app makes the moment a session's start has returned, if its lifecycle still reads `resumed` then — every Android return to the foreground starts a session, and so does every iOS one with background sharing off — and, for a session whose start returned before the app was resumed, by the heal the next `resumed` event runs; so the wait ends at the next visit that outlasts the session's start, and what remains is the relay's own schedule. A visit that ends while the start is still in flight claims nothing. In the poll configuration (`HAVEN_LIVE_SYNC=false`) that drive is the bridge's resume on the foreground health tick, on the claim the tick reads (`resume_driven`). A process whose lifecycle never reads `resumed` — which on Android includes a Haven window that stays visible but unfocused — makes no drive in the full mode. A session open in another isolate — the foreground service's, a background worker's — writes that record too, and drives there only to finish. Until a drive, such a circle neither sends nor reads on this device, what it receives meanwhile is stored without a cap, and it is NOT named by half (b): the reporter reads the engine's verdict only. An admin's removal is dead on this device either way — without the record every convergence pass of the circle fails on the unpublished commit — so the record costs that circle nothing and is what lets the foreground drive resolve it. AN EVICTION a kill left staged is given NO record: without one the circle reads stable and heals when another remaining member's eviction for the same departure is applied here, and under a record it would not until a drive resolved it, which exists in one receive configuration and one lifecycle only (`an_eviction_a_kill_left_with_no_record_is_healed_by_another_members_commit`); where this device is the only remaining member nothing heals it. AN EVICTION KILLED INSIDE ITS OWN STAGING leaves a circle that reads healthy, names nothing in any store, and cannot share from this device until a commit of that circle is applied here; half (b) does not name it — the send that fails is answered typed (`CircleError::SendBlockedByDeparture`) and no screen maps that yet (`an_eviction_killed_inside_its_staging_leaves_a_circle_that_cannot_share_and_says_why`). And A CHANGE THAT REMOVES NOBODY, killed before it was recorded, is cleared at the next open: it never left the device, and its stored row is retired before the session's first engine call, so no pass applies it on this device alone (`a_commit_cleared_at_open_is_retired_and_never_merged`; a row a record still names may be held by a relay and stays). The circle is told the change was undone (`ChangeNote::ChangeUndone`) — written from what is stored, in the pass before the open, so a process that ends before the engine's own one-time announcement is collected has still said so; best-effort — which the circle's change card in Circle details shows (`changeNoteChangeUndone`). The repair is held to an admin's own removal, and to exactly this, by `the_live_planes_foreground_is_the_one_product_driver_and_the_open_repairs_a_removal_only`, which fails when the repair's coverage changes or anything of the driver is named in haven-core or the bridge outside the driver, the catch-up plane and the live plane's one foreground drive. WHAT THE FOREGROUND DRIVE LEAVES: a circle with a commit awaiting its relays when the app goes to the background is not driven again until a caller next claims the foreground — the claim behind a session start or the heal in a resumed app, a foreground open, a health tick that carries the claim — and does not share from the background meanwhile — each background send for it is answered with the typed deferral and an empty hand-back, nothing is retried in a loop, and the user is told what any deferred send tells them and no more: the sharing-health model's deferred-send verdict when the send was the foreground's, the missing publish acknowledgement it reads at the next foreground open when it was the background's — neither says a commit is awaiting its relays (`a_location_send_for_a_circle_awaiting_its_relay_is_deferred_typed_and_touches_nothing`); a session whose start returns while the app is not resumed — a launch behind a system dialog, a return through the app switcher, a visit that ended while the start was in flight, a process the operating system launched in the background, and on Android a window that is visible but unfocused — records and drives nothing until a caller claims the foreground for it: the heal at the next `resumed` event (which every resume runs, behind any start still in flight), a foreground open, or a health tick that finds the app resumed; and while an Android window stays unfocused no health tick runs either, so nothing does until the user touches Haven. A session whose start returns while the app IS resumed is claimed for at once. A process whose lifecycle never reads `resumed` is never claimed; a live session's open-time advance of every circle runs BEFORE any claim and is the inputs-only one, so it releases nothing — a due eviction and a leave to be minted again wait for the claim's drive, which makes them under a record — and what a started session RECEIVES is taken in the mode that makes no commit, as is what the wake's catch-up sweep releases. And A CHANGE OF THE GROUP LEFT QUEUED would hold its circle at its epoch on every plane that does not make the engine's full advance — once the circle's convergence pass has closed the engine applies nothing it receives until that change has had its one attempt — so such a plane retires it, its circle told first, once input waits behind it, and the device moves with its circle (`a_change_left_queued_is_retired_and_told_when_a_commit_waits_behind_it_on_a_plane_that_does_not_drive`). The driver's entries answer a change the engine queued as `Queued`, typed, and the live plane's foreground drive gives a queued one its attempt. Every session open that has a store for its notes, in every configuration and before any advance, retires each change of a group it finds queued, its circle told first (`ChangeNote::QueuedChangeDropped`; one whose circle cannot be told is kept, one that could not be deleted is not said to have been, and a session with nowhere durable to keep the note retires none). It runs after the removal repair, so a queued removal whose own commit was just given its record goes without a word, and neither stops the other when it fails: nothing the app calls leaves one queued on purpose (`no_product_path_leaves_a_group_change_queued`), so one found there is what a take-back the store refused, or a process that died between the engine's queue write and the take-back, left behind an answer that said it was not made. A finish-only call, which can never make the full advance, retires one at the moment it is what holds the circle still — input waiting, no pass open to take it up — with the same note. That test can answer no for a circle that IS held: the engine also reports a pass as due while canonical applications are pending, and a circle the reservation holds can be in that state, so its queued change stays queued and the circle stays at its epoch. It never answers yes because the store could not be read. What still stands, within one session, is a take-back the store refused — told to its circle (`ChangeNote::QueuedChangesHeld`) — on a plane that makes no full advance: a session nobody has claimed the foreground for, a background burst, the wake's catch-up sweep. And WHAT THE ENGINE LEAVES STRANDED IS DETECTED, SAID AND HANDED BACK — with limits. While a commit of this device's is pending the engine stores, unopened, every `kind:445` of that circle that arrives — a fix, a proposal and a peer's commit alike, and, the gate being ahead of any authentication, whatever anybody who knows the circle's routing tag sends under it — and reads those rows again only at the end of a confirm, of a rollback and of a join. A row left in that state in a circle that holds no pending commit is stranded: delivered by nothing until this device next confirms or rolls back a commit of its own in that circle — a re-join ends a row from before the new copy's join epoch undelivered —, answered as buffered at every redelivery meanwhile, and behind any earlier row that goes on failing to replay. Seven ways leave one, six reproduced on the real engine: a process that dies after a confirm's transaction; one that dies after a rollback's; the engine's own clearing of a staged commit at an open; a replayed row that errors, with no death at all; the engine's sweep of a deferred row failing on it, with no pending commit involved; the engine's own replay having no room for a row it cannot open, which anyone who knows the routing tag can bring about; and, read and not run, a re-join that dies before its replay (`stranded_input_measured_e2e.rs`, `a_fix_parked_behind_a_pending_commit_is_stranded_by_a_kill_until_this_devices_next_confirm`). What it costs was measured: a fix is one missed fix; a peer's commit leaves this device an epoch behind, unable to read what follows and sealing what a member that commit removed can still read; a rival commit the circle kept leaves it alone on a branch of its own; a leave makes the eviction that names it unappliable here for good, and this device's own next rollback then ends it on another branch at the same epoch number — alone there when its key is the higher of the two committers', joined by each member handed its eviction when it is the lower. Haven reads the engine's store for such rows — a group event exactly as it arrived, awaiting a retry, that the engine does not hold as processed, in a circle the OPEN engine reports stable and this device is still in (`stranded_rows`, `replays_nothing`) — at every open, after every confirm and rollback it asks of the engine, and wherever a redelivery is answered from one. It says so durably BEFORE it does anything (`ChangeNote::UnreadChange` for an event that by its stored tags CLAIMS to be a commit or a proposal, `ChangeNote::UnreadLocation` for a fix; read through `SessionManager::peek_change_notes`; no screen shows either yet): that input is waiting unread, never that the circle is out of step, since nothing in an unopened event is authenticated and anybody who knows the routing tag can have sent it. Then, at the top of every call that hands the engine an event, advances a circle, or seals or stages for one, and ahead of anything newly delivered, it hands them back (`hand_back_stranded`) — the call's own circle first, at most 256 of its events a call and sixteen for a call that makes no commit and runs inside a wake or runs beside one, every other circle sharing one slice of sixteen: the signed event is verified and kept in Haven's own store (`kept_input` in the encrypted circle database: ciphertext as a relay served it, nothing decrypted), the engine's row is released through MDK's own `release_message_for_replay`, the event is ingested through the same screen and the same engine call a relay's delivery takes, and the kept copy is destroyed on an answer that says the engine judged it or holds it again. A death at any point of that loses nothing, repeats nothing and keeps the order. What the engine makes of it is folded by the plane that was calling, in its own lifecycle — a finish-only plane records and stages nothing for it. The hand-back itself contacts no relay. While the call's own circle still holds input the hand-back can take and has not — the call's room ran out, the circle's cap stands, the engine's store refused a release, or a store could not be read or written before a row was taken over — nothing new of that circle is taken, sealed or staged: an ingest's caller holds its cursor, a location send is answered deferred and a change of the group held, each typed, and the next call carries on. Each such hold ends by something that happens — room, at the next call; the cap, when an entry ends, which every call tries while it stands; a store, when it answers — whoever parked what: an event the engine has no room for is not kept once its id is on record as owed its refetch, and neither is one the engine erred on AFTER writing its own record of it, which a member, or one since removed who still holds the epoch's key, can send without number; so with N events parked ahead of a stranded removal that removal is handed back within ⌈(N+1)/256⌉ calls in the foreground and ⌈(N+1)/16⌉ in a burst or beside one, and no location is sealed for the removed member meanwhile. What the engine has no room for, and what it defers and later lets go, is refetched by id like any other object it refused, on a wait that doubles from a minute to a day and forgets nothing — no count of tries and no count of epochs ends an owed id, so a device many commits behind with no room left still reaches its circle's epoch (`INV-R-BACKGROUND-PRESENCE-ONLY-AT-PUBLISH` gives the bound and the request pattern). An event is handed back whatever its tags say — a NIP-40 expiration is unauthenticated and decides nothing — and an old fix handed back never displaces a newer one of the same member. What is kept is destroyed with its circle, with the whole store at logout, and when this device is found removed. NOT repaired: a session with no durable store is told, releases nothing and holds nothing; a circle holds at most 256 kept events or 4 MiB — only what the engine has not yet been asked about and what it erred on with NO record of its own count: the engine errs on an ingest for a fault of its own store, or after it has written its own record of the event, and the second kind ends where it is handed back — the engine holds its id as processed — so no sender, a member or a removed one included, fills the cap, and only a fault of this device's own store can — and while that cap stands what is past it stays with the engine, told, and the circle's own calls are answered held, each asking the engine again for what fills it, until that store answers; a row that is not a verifiable event is left and holds nothing; one whose release the engine's store refuses is left, with no copy kept beside it, and holds its circle's calls until the store takes the release; an event the engine errs on with no record of its own is never given up on, on a count of tries or of epochs — it is asked for once at each look (an open, a confirm or rollback, a change of the circle's epoch), keeps its circle told, and ends when the engine answers for it or its circle is left: how far the circle has moved says nothing about an event nobody opened; a kept copy that is no longer its event does not stay — beside the engine's row it ends and the row is taken over afresh, and with no row left it ends with its id owed its refetch; a circle the engine reports halted, or one this device was removed from, is not touched; nothing SCHEDULES a hand-back — a row waits for the next call for its circle on this device, the open-time advance of every circle being the first; and what a stranded row already cost is not undone — an eviction set aside while the leave it names could not be taken over stays set aside. A redelivery answered from a stranded row Haven can hand back to nobody — one that is not a verifiable event — holds no cursor (`ReceiveOnlyOutcome::Stranded`), while one that arrives for a circle whose rows could not be kept or read is held with that circle's other calls until the store answers: the answer is the stored row's and the same every time, and before this a row left by a rollback or by the open's clear — stored under the circle's CURRENT epoch — held both planes' cursors, so a commit or a proposal, which carry no expiration, was fetched again at every sweep. It is the engine's behaviour in every mode, and a deviation from the protocol's durability rules. It is why a finish-only drive still leaves every confirm to a full one — which defers the same confirm, lets more be parked meanwhile, and leaves a circle with a commit awaiting its relays not sharing from the background, acknowledged or not. And A LEAVE THE ENGINE MINTED AGAIN, handed back by a hold after the foreground it began under had ended, is dropped rather than kept for a later foreground, and in a circle that reaches no next epoch it is not proposed again: the engine notes the epoch it proposed the leave at before it hands the proposal over, and proposes once per epoch. The user who left is then silent and stays on every roster until that circle's epoch moves (`a_proposal_handed_back_after_the_foreground_ended_is_not_kept`). And THREE HOLDS A PASS AWAY FROM THE FOREGROUND LEAVES cost that circle its sharing from everywhere but a claimed foreground, with nothing shown. (1) A change of the circle's relays whose confirm a finish-only pass FINISHED: each send that is not a claimed foreground's is answered deferred, typed (`SendHeld::AwaitsForeground`), until a full drive has completed in a claimed foreground. That drive is ALL it waits for: a circle's subscription follows its routing by itself (whichever plane moves a circle's row — the live receive, the live drive's confirm, a bridge `*_driven` entry, catch-up — wakes the live session's follow, which moves the circle's REQ (`LiveSyncCore::follow_routing`) in a claimed foreground and in a burst, and once more as a burst opens; nothing in the app calls it and the FFI entry is gone; a circle whose move fails stays listed and the next health tick a claimed foreground makes, or the next burst open, issues its REQ; a relay the circle left is listed for that REQ for a day from this device's record of the change and is then fetched by id only, decision 237 — the session wakes its follow when the day ends, so the REQ there ends and its socket closes then, in a running process; one suspended across it ends the REQ at its next wake or open; a `nostr_group_id` rotation another client's admin makes is followed the same way, in one transaction with its prior routing, and a follow a kill or an error missed is made at the next start, sweep or burst open; a rotation or a Welcome onto an id another circle on the device holds holds both circles until each is left, T-ROUTING-ROTATION), and a device that APPLIES a peer's change of relays in a burst is not held at all — the lifecycle batch's. (2) A queued REMOVAL of a member still listed, retired unmade by a pass that makes no full advance or by the sweep at a session's open: each such send is answered deferred (`SendHeld::RemovalUnmade`) while a member it named is still listed and its note (`ChangeNote::QueuedRemovalDropped`) stands. No screen reads that note and nothing acknowledges it (W14, before a release); nothing asks for the removal again by itself as shipped ("offered", decision 233, `REQUEUE_SET_ASIDE_REMOVALS` false): the members stay held and the note stands until the user removes them again. A withdrawn removal of this device's own is held the same way: never handed to MDK's re-issue, which would remove a member invited back since, but dropped as an offer with every member it named kept with its asks spent and both notes said before MDK's record is deleted — unless none of them is on the applied, stable roster, when it asked for what is already so and is deleted unsaid, as MDK's own `AlreadySatisfied`. The automatic posture the owner may still choose asks a full drive, once the circle is caught up, stable and free of any other own commit or queued change, and not being left, for the removal again for the members still listed whom no applied commit took out, while this device is an admin — by Haven's own bound, per member at most twice (counted once a commit is staged under a record), none once the circle has moved more than MDK's rewind horizon past the epoch the removal was set aside at, and none for a set-aside copy MDK had itself re-issued; past a bound the members stay held and the note stays for the user (decision 180). (3) A commit recorded in the foreground that no relay may hold: a drive that only finishes gives it no first transmission, so it stays pending for as long as the app stays away, and its circle is SILENT (`SendHeld::AwaitingRelays`) and DEAF — the engine parks everything the circle sends, unopened and with no cap, another admin's removal included — until the app is opened and a full drive sends it. Accepted as the careful side of that trade (an owner decision is recorded): the other side is a first transmission the operating system can cut. BOTH of the first two holds are read by every call that is not a claimed foreground's, and the second by that one too. In a process with NO live plane — the poll configuration, the Android service's isolate, the app's own before its session is claimed — a call is a claimed foreground's only while a bridge call made on its caller's foreground claim stands behind it (`SessionManager::away_from_the_foreground`): the absence of a claim is read as its absence, never as a claim, and the Android service makes none. So the poll configuration ends a relay-change mark at a full drive in front of its user — the foreground health tick's resume — as a live-sync build does, and the Android service's isolate reads both holds. And A LEAVE holds its circle for EVERY call, a claimed foreground's included — on the driver's entries `Publishing::leave` / `resume_leave`, the only ones the app's leave takes (`leave_driven` at the press, `resume_leave_driven` at every wake: the health tick, the start-up's and the resume's relay contact while the app reads `resumed`, each iOS burst, each Android foreground-service cycle and each WorkManager wake): from the instant the intent is written, before the engine is asked, no call seals a location of the circle (`SendHeld::Leaving`, read again after the seal's hand-back), the driver sends no recorded one whose pre-send check finds the intent, and a location record not yet sent is deleted, until `resume_leave` finds the copy marked removed, or a day passed since the first press or since the latest press that found no proposal ever minted, or the intent more than an hour ahead of a stepped-back clock — Rust arms no timer for it — or the engine refuses the leave for good, which ends the intent; an intent the store cannot read holds. Every app plane seals and sends through the driver's entries, so a location sealed before the press is not sent after it. A promotion of this device taken in between the leave's plan and its proposal no longer ends the leave: the driver keeps the intent, plans again and steps down before it proposes (`a_promotion_taken_in_between_the_plan_and_the_proposal_is_stepped_down_from`) — in a full drive; a wake's carry-on answers that it waits for one, with the intent kept. `AdminMustStepDown` is reachable only from `propose_leave`, which no app plane calls. The user sees the circle stop sharing, which is what Leave asked for; no screen says the leave is still in progress (W14).

invariants.title: Each circle is an independent MLS group with its own keys
invariants.statement: Two circles never share key material or a group identifier, and ciphertext produced in one circle is undecryptable by a member of another even when that member is in both; deriving any circle's keys from a shared or account-level secret falsifies this.

event_kinds.note: The per-circle ciphertext whose cross-group undecryptability this invariant asserts.

invariants.title: MLS signing keys are never the Nostr identity key
invariants.statement: The MLS leaf signature key and the Nostr identity key can never be the same key, structurally: ciphersuite 0x0001 fixes the leaf signature scheme to Ed25519 while the Nostr identity is secp256k1 Schnorr. The account-identity proof does NOT enforce inequality — validate_leaf_account_identity_proof authenticates the binding (a proof binding a key to itself would verify) — so the engine rejecting an unverifiable proof is not what makes this true.

event_kinds.note: Built by AccountIdentityProofRequest::proof_event() in cgka-engine, reached from the IN-TREE call site haven-core/src/nostr/mls/signer.rs. NOT the peeler. Never published. Note the shipped code (v2 / 0xF2F1 / kind-450-framed) diverges from foundation/account-identity-proof-v1.md, which specifies v0x01 and says the proof is not a Nostr event at all — a spec catch-up would be a wire-format change.

invariants.title: Every kind-445 carries a fresh, single-use author key
invariants.statement: Each group message is signed by a newly generated keypair, so no two location events share an author pubkey and none of them is the sender's identity key; reusing a keypair across messages, or letting the exporter-derived ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce repeat under one epoch key, falsifies this. A location is offered to a relay once: one whose send a process died inside is deleted by the next drive, never sent again and never sealed again to look new.

event_kinds.note: wire_allowlist.json marks this kind ephemeral_pubkey:true, which the wire-journal oracle enforces on real published events.

invariants.title: Keys change on membership change or an explicit repair, never on a timer
invariants.statement: Periodic self-update (MIP-03 SHOULD) is disabled. A joiner makes the one post-join self-update MDK records, once, in a foreground full drive after catch-up; it holds the joiner's location sends as awaiting relays until a relay acknowledges it, and on an upgraded install each joined circle makes its one self-update a CSPRNG gap of 2-30 s after the previous one, so two circles' commits never share a second while all of them land within minutes - a residual timing linkage a relay archive holding two of them can still read. Any member may tap Repair on a circle whose delivery broke: a real self-update, rate-limited to one per circle per 24 h by the epoch-age gate and reachable only from the bridge's driven entry. At code level an admin's commits also advance an epoch (a membership change, a relay-list update, each half of an admin handoff). Keys change on a membership change, one's own join or an explicit repair, NEVER on a timer: no wake, timer or drain authors a self-update, MDK's queued self-updates are retired in the hold that queued them and before every full advance, and no periodic or manual maintenance is ever enrolled. scripts/ci/check_self_update_sites.sh holds the construction to one site and its callers to the repair and the post-join; scripts/ci/check_epoch_repair_isolation.sh and haven/test/lints/self_update_disabled_test.dart keep the Dart repair user-triggered and foreground-only.

invariants.title: Removing a member advances the epoch and locks them out of new location
invariants.statement: An ADMIN removal is a commit that advances the group epoch, and a member removed at epoch N cannot decrypt a location published at epoch N+1; the commit is applied only after at least one relay acked it, so a member is never treated as removed on a commit nobody received.

event_kinds.note: Removal commits ride the same kind as application messages, distinguished only by the absence of the expiration tag.

tests.name: the dialog states the consequence before anything is staged
a failed removal leaves the roster and the caches alone

The SELF-LEAVE path (which the Privacy-page sentence covered until the page was removed on 2026-08-29) has an accepted unconverged case (deviation LEAVE-GHOST) where the ghost stays authorized until a manual admin removal; that removal is now an affordance an admin actually has (the member row's remove button, shipped 2026-08-15), where before it existed only as a service with no caller. invariants.title: A commit that removes a member is never undone because no relay could be reached
invariants.statement: A commit under a durable fanout record that removes a member — an admin's removal or the eviction of a member who left — is never undone because no relay could be reached, however long that lasts: it stays pending, and while it does THIS DEVICE shares nothing with anybody, the removed member included; the other members go on encrypting to the old roster until the commit reaches them. Only a commit KNOWN to remove nobody is undone when no relay took it within a day, and known means a mark written in the lock hold that staged the commit, cleared before every record of its circle is written — a record the open writes included — and withheld from a circle that held, when the hold began, a proposal the commit could have taken in; a missing mark, or one that cannot be read, reads as a commit that may remove a member. A record the open wrote for a commit it found staged is protected by a second mechanism as well: every relay it names is stored as one that may hold the commit, and a commit a relay may hold is never bounded. Undoing a removal for want of a reachable relay, treating an unmarked commit as one that removes nobody, or letting an earlier commit's mark stand for a later commit of its circle, falsifies this. What CAN undo a removal is every frozen relay's proven refusal, which is INV-L-WEDGED-CIRCLE-IS-DETECTED-AND-NAMED's clause, not this one.
invariants.residual: Scoped to commits under a durable fanout record — since W9q every commit is staged under one, and no plane publishes through a ladder — and to the drive that applies the bound, which is one in the full mode only: the live plane's while its session's lifecycle is `Foreground` — entered only on a caller's claim, which the Dart layer makes from the strict `resumed` read and from nothing else (INV-L-WEDGED-CIRCLE-IS-DETECTED-AND-NAMED) — or, where no live plane runs, a bridge driven entry's on its caller's foreground claim. The withholding of the mark from a circle that holds a committable proposal (`SessionManager::roster_before`) is exercised for one state that produces it — a leaver's proposal left in the proposal store by a process that died while staging its eviction, reproduced on the real engine. A second is closed by construction rather than reproduced: with a fairness slot the engine prepares a queued admin change ahead of a due eviction, and such a change might take in by reference a leave that was not yet stored when the hold began, which the roster read before the call cannot show. So a commit the engine RELEASED from its queue is never marked as removing nobody, whatever the rosters say (`SessionManager::stage_commits`). The cost: a released change that removes nobody and that no relay takes is never undone at its bound either — it stays pending until a relay answers.

invariants.title: A joiner receives current-epoch keys only and no replayed history
invariants.statement: A member added at epoch N cannot DECRYPT any kind-445 sealed before the commit that added them, regardless of what a relay serves: the Welcome conveys only the current epoch's joiner_secret path and the MLS key schedule is one-way, so no earlier exporter_secret is derivable. Haven additionally has no backfill path — the Add stages no application message and the welcome ingest carries no location results.
invariants.note: Delivery of pre-join ciphertext to a joiner is REACHABLE and harmless: SEED_LOOKBACK_SECS = 86_400 (relay/live_sync/session.rs:54) seeds a new circle's kind-445 cursor to now-24h rather than to the join epoch, so the first sweep's REQ window legitimately covers up to a day before the join. The 228 s NIP-40 expiration means a conformant relay holds almost nothing that old, but a buggy or hostile one may serve it. The claim holds because the ciphertext is UNREADABLE, not because it is never delivered — which is exactly what the cited test pins, by handing the joiner the real pre-join event through process_event.

invariants.title: Exactly five past epochs of exporter secrets are retained
invariants.statement: The engine keeps DEFAULT_MAX_PAST_EPOCHS = 5 past epochs' exporter secrets and its application-message accept window equals that bound, so a ciphertext exactly at the window edge still decrypts and one past it does not; widening the window keeps stale secrets alive, narrowing it drops legitimate offline backlog, and either direction fails the pin.

invariants.title: Every co-member learns your Nostr identity public key
invariants.statement: Each MLS leaf carries a kind-450 account-identity proof binding the member to their Nostr identity key, and the engine rejects a leaf whose proof does not verify, so joining a circle necessarily discloses that pubkey to every other member and to everyone already in the circle; there is no pseudonymous-within-circle mode.

event_kinds.note: Built by AccountIdentityProofRequest::proof_event() in cgka-engine, reached from the IN-TREE call site haven-core/src/nostr/mls/signer.rs. NOT the peeler. Never published. Note the shipped code (v2 / 0xF2F1 / kind-450-framed) diverges from foundation/account-identity-proof-v1.md, which specifies v0x01 and says the proof is not a Nostr event at all — a spec catch-up would be a wire-format change.

invariants.title: A kind-445 carries h and expiration and no other tag
invariants.statement: Published group events carry only the h routing tag (plus a NIP-40 expiration on application messages); no alt tag, no geohash g tag and no client tag ever reaches a relay — in particular the dead local 445 builder at nostr/event.rs, which stamps alt and a truncated 5-char geohash, must stay unreachable.

event_kinds.note: wire_allowlist.json pins tags.allowed = [h, expiration] and tags.required = [h, expiration]; a geohash or alt tag landing on the wire is a violation.
Read-side subscription filter for the group plane (live_sync/planes/group.rs:14) — same kind, spelled as a numeric literal rather than reached through the peeler.

invariants.title: Every kind-445 application message this device publishes carries a NIP-40 expiry of at most 228 s; control messages carry none
invariants.statement: Every kind-445 APPLICATION message THIS DEVICE publishes carries a NIP-40 `expiration` of inner_created_at + at most LOCATION_MESSAGE_RETENTION_SECS (228 s), in EVERY circle — including one created by a client that declared no message-retention.v1 component (0x8005), where the engine would stamp nothing: the installed peeler (RetentionBoundPeeler) supplies Haven's own window when the group declares none or zero, caps a longer group policy to it, and honours a shorter one as declared. This device never stamps a commit or proposal, so among the 445s THIS device sends, the absence of an expiration identifies a group-control message. That inference does NOT extend to the circle's whole #h stream: in a circle declaring no component, another member's unstamped 445 may be a location update (see residual). The tag set on this device's 445s is exactly `h` for control and `h` + `expiration` for application messages — nothing else.

event_kinds.note: The engine derives the expiration from the group component; Haven's send path takes no per-send expiration.
Welcome gift wraps carry no expiration — the invitation may sit on an inbox relay indefinitely.

invariants.residual: Bounded to the traffic THIS device authors, which is all it can bound. In a circle created by a client that declared no 0x8005 component, another member's own location 445s still carry no expiration: they may be retained indefinitely AND, to any relay watching the circle's public #h, they are indistinguishable from membership changes — so in such a mixed circle the un-stamped class contains another member's LOCATION UPDATES, not only control messages. The un-stamped class is every group-control message, not membership alone — an admin handoff and a relay-set change are UpdateAppComponents commits and are un-stamped too, which is what `expiration_separates_location_from_control_and_no_other_tag_appears` actually publishes. The Privacy-page sentence that stated this discriminator (scoped to the messages this device sends) was removed with the page on 2026-08-29; SECURITY.md's discriminator bullet is now its only statement. Haven still cannot repair the group itself: writing the component is admin-gated upstream (require_admin on the UpdateAppComponents path) and a joiner is not an admin, and doing it inside the join path would stage an epoch-advancing commit whose non-publication pins the group in PendingPublish and buffers every inbound message forever, which is a worse loss than the leak. The residue is disclosed nowhere: nothing in the app tells the user that in such a circle another member's location 445s may sit on a relay indefinitely and read as group control — and since the owner removed the in-app explanation layer on 2026-08-29 there is no surface left to disclose it on, so it is recorded in SECURITY.md rather than held open as a copy decision. SECOND: the bound MASKS the group-level declaration, and it masks it in three pre-existing proofs, not one. `seal_location_attaches_group_retention_expiration` and `expired_tag_does_not_block_ingest` (src/circle/manager.rs) and the E2E wire oracle (tooling/e2e/wire_allowlist.json, kind 445 `required: [h, expiration]`) all now pass with create_group's 0x8005 declaration removed, because the bound supplies the tag they look for; `live_sync_cursor_replay_e2e.rs`'s expiration precondition is masked the same way. NOTHING AT THE WIRE LEVEL still proves Haven declares 0x8005 to its peers, and the component is the only thing governing every OTHER member's client. Held at host level instead, by `a_locally_created_circle_declares_havens_retention_window_to_every_member` (both parties read the window back out of group state) and `a_shorter_group_policy_reaches_the_wire_as_declared` (a foreign circle's narrower window reaches the wire as declared, which the bound could not fake). Closing it on the wire needs an allow-list entry that asserts the delta VALUE against the circle's declared window rather than the tag's presence — owned by the E2E lane, not by this crate. THIRD: the bound honours an arbitrarily short declared window, so a circle whose creator declares e.g. 1 s has every Haven member's location dropped by a NIP-40-honouring relay almost immediately. Deliberately not floored — a floor would ask relays to hold location ciphertext LONGER than the circle declared, and would not restore visibility, since the same component governs every other member's client. SECURITY.md's no-gap invariant is scoped to circles Haven created for exactly this reason — and, since PUB-COALESCE, to rosters of at most kMaxCirclesPerBurst circles as well — which is every roster the app admits, because kMaxCirclesPerAccount (10) refuses the eleventh (INV-W-445-EXPIRATION-WINDOW). That window is no longer undisclosed: the circle-details subtitle reports the EFFECTIVE window for the messages this device sends into that circle — in seconds when it is under a minute, so a narrow foreign window reads as alarming rather than being rounded away — held by INV-U-CIRCLE-EXPIRY-SHOWN-IS-EXPIRY-SENT. What the sheet does not say is WHY it is short: it reports the number, not that another client chose it. SCOPE NOTE (Bluetooth mesh, opt-in): the expiration bounds what RELAYS are asked to keep, not what the mesh carries. With mesh on, the same signed event travels inside a packet whose own lifetime is twenty minutes, and a phone that carried it keeps it in an unread queue until its app reads it — so the ciphertext is held by phones in radio range past the instant relays drop it, by design (docs/BLUETOOTH_MESH_PLAN.md §6.4). The expiration is inside the signed event and nothing extends it; a member that takes the event in late judges its age by the MLS-authenticated inner timestamp. No radio is built yet, so no packet leaves a device in any shipped build.

invariants.title: The relay-residency window Haven asks for is the CEILING the copy states, and the smallest the no-gap floor allows — at every roster the account bound admits
invariants.statement: LOCATION_MESSAGE_RETENTION_SECS is the CEILING on the NIP-40 window Haven requests, not the window every message carries: an application kind-445 gets it whenever the group declares no message-retention.v1 (0x8005) window, declares zero, or declares a LONGER one, while a SHORTER declared window is honoured as declared (bounded_retention_secs — see INV-W-445-EXPIRATION-SCOPE for the per-message rule and INV-U-CIRCLE-EXPIRY-SHOWN-IS-EXPIRY-SENT for what the user is shown). The constant equals kLocationPublishMaxInterval + 2 * kTtlNetworkBufferSeconds read out of haven/lib/src/constants/location.dart. Three things therefore move together: the no-widening bound (a larger window leaves every published location on relays longer than the design commits to), the no-narrowing bound (a smaller one leaves a member returning from offline with nothing unexpired left to fetch), and the honouring of a shorter declared window (a flat figure would be false in every circle another client created with a narrower window, which is the circle whose window the user cannot change; the wire-level proof is INV-W-445-EXPIRATION-SCOPE's a_shorter_group_policy_reaches_the_wire_as_declared, and the effective figure the user still sees is the circle-details subtitle, INV-U-CIRCLE-EXPIRY-SHOWN-IS-EXPIRY-SENT). The Privacy-page sentence that quoted the figure ('about four minutes', as an 'at most' bound) was removed with the page on 2026-08-29 and its copy-tie tests with it; SECURITY.md carries the derivation. Editing the constant, the Dart publish ceiling, or the honouring of a shorter declared window without the others fails. The no-gap floor the ceiling is sized against is a bound on the SCHEDULED gap and it holds for rosters up to kMaxCirclesPerBurst (11): one coalesced burst per interval publishes every eligible circle (PUB-COALESCE), so a circle that leads one burst and trails the next waits kLocationPublishMaxInterval (168 s) plus at most one burst spread (kPublishStaggerMaxSpread, 30 s) = 198 s, leaving the whole 30 s of kTtlNetworkBufferSeconds unspent. From the twelfth circle up the burst would defer its tail and that floor would no longer hold, which is why the ROSTER is bounded below the burst cap: kMaxCirclesPerAccount (10) refuses circle creation and invitation accept — the only two operations that CREATE a circles row — at the one seam both reach the core through, so the floor holds at every roster a user can have and the ceil(N / kMaxCirclesPerBurst) service-period ladder is unreachable in production. What this entry does NOT promise is the propagation margin its predecessor had: the burst spread spends one of the two kTtlNetworkBufferSeconds, so the margin is 30 s and not 60 s at every roster from two circles up, and the residual says so — as it does for the three REALIZED-gap terms that sit outside this SCHEDULED bound, TWO of which cross the retention at rosters this bound admits.

invariants.residual: The no-gap property this constant is sized for is a bound on the SCHEDULED gap, and it is bounded by the ROSTER at eleven circles — which is why the roster itself is bounded at TEN. kMaxCirclesPerAccount (owner decision, 2026-09-09) refuses circle creation and invitation accept once the account holds ten accepted circles, enforced in NostrCircleService because its two roster-growing calls are the only Dart callers of the only two core operations that CREATE a circles row: create_circle_with_config, which upserts through CircleStorage::save_circle, and record_processed_invitation, which runs its own INSERT INTO circles. 'CREATE' and not 'write' is the property, and the difference is load-bearing rather than pedantic: save_circle is an UPSERT with three further non-test callers (resync_circle_relays_from_mdk, add_members, remove_members), and record_processed_invitation is not among them; each of those three reads the row back with storage.get_circle first and returns early when there is none, so none of them can mint one. The gate is also enforced against CONCURRENCY, not only against call sites: _refuseIfRosterFull RESERVES the admitted slot (_reservedRosterSlots, released in the caller's finally), because the row only exists once the core write returns, so without the reservation simultaneous accepts would each read the same pre-growth roster and enough of them would carry it past kMaxCirclesPerBurst — the deferral the bound exists to eliminate. The call-site half is pinned by 'only the gated service grows the account roster' (haven/test/lints/circle_roster_bound_sites_test.dart), an AST inventory over all of lib minus lib/src/rust/ — main.dart included, with its own anti-vacuity assertion — which fails on a third call site rather than letting one land silently; the concurrency half by 'admit exactly one when only one slot is left' and its two slot-release siblings. A burst is therefore never handed more than ten circles and the deferral ladder below is UNREACHABLE in production. THE LADDER IS KEPT ON RECORD BECAUSE THE DEFERRAL CODE IS, and lifting the bound re-opens it verbatim: a burst publishes at most kMaxCirclesPerBurst (11) circles and defers the rest to the next tick, _takeBurstSlice is strict round-robin, so a DEFERRED circle's worst SERVICE PERIOD would be ceil(N / 11) bursts rather than two at every roster — N = 12..22 -> TWO sampled intervals (144 s best, 240 s mean, 336 s worst, and 366 s once the burst-position differential is added, because a circle may lead one burst and trail the one two ticks later, a whole kPublishStaggerMaxSpread apart); N = 23..33 -> three (216 / 360 / 504 s); N >= 34 -> four or more, where even the BEST case (288 s) exceeds the 228 s retention on EVERY publish rather than on some. Both halves stay PINNED rather than left as prose, so that a lifted bound cannot re-open them unmeasured: the round-robin period by 'a deferred circle waits ceil(N / kMaxCirclesPerBurst) bursts' (which drives real ticks through _takeBurstSlice, so it fails when the slice size or the rotate moves) and the seconds by 'and past the cap, the deferral ladder in SECONDS' (which reads them off the cadence constants, so it fails when the cadence moves). The two scope limits that used to matter go with it: a tick folding into a running iOS burst (BackgroundBurstCoordinator._joinable), and the 21-circle point where a one-shot's own spread outlasts kLocationPublishOverlapGuard, are both reachable only at N >= 12. WHAT THE BOUND DOES NOT CLOSE, and what this entry therefore does not promise. FIRST, the PROPAGATION MARGIN. Against the ACTUAL predecessor — per-circle schedulers, where the gap was each circle's own sampled interval, <= 168 s at every N, with no spread and no deferral — the full 60 s (2 x kTtlNetworkBufferSeconds) was margin; since PUB-COALESCE the burst spread spends one of the two, so this invariant runs on 30 s of propagation and clock-skew margin at every roster from TWO circles up. That halving is not a past-eleven effect and the roster bound does not touch it; it is recorded in the ratchet_override block for PUB-COALESCE, the change that caused it, so it sits in a reviewed diff and not only here. SECOND, the period is a period of TURNS, and a turn is a SELECTION rather than a publish: the rotation advances when the tick FIRES, ahead of the chain, the window and the sink, so a slice that loses its window (no identity, disclosure not accepted, a fix that timed out, a pause under it, an iOS coordinator that drops a queued burst) publishes nothing and waits a whole interval over again — up to 336 s against this 228 s retention, at every roster including a bounded one. The health model is told; the queue is not. THIRD, THREE REALIZED-gap terms sit outside this SCHEDULED bound, and two of them cross the retention at rosters the bound admits. The Android foreground service publishes on a platform delivery that arrives a TTFF late: on API 23-30 a cold acquisition reaches 248 s, i.e. 20 s past this 228 s, pinned by equality per API regime in haven/test/services/background_fix_request_test.dart. The iOS burst HEAD (connect, backlog wait and one-shot fix, up to 40 s) varies between bursts and so enters the realized gap as a differential on top of the spread: 168 + 40 + spread reaches 235 s at four circles and 238 s from five up, so iOS is inside 228 s only up to three circles. The THIRD is the only one that scales with N and coalescing introduced it: the pass is SERIAL and the stagger buys separation on top of each publish rather than inside it, so the foreground _pacedPublish — which measures the gap from the previous publish's START — spans sum(max(gap_i, dur_i)), while the background pass awaits the gap AFTER the previous publish returns and is strictly additive, sum(dur_i + gap_i+1); at one publish priced at kBurstPublishBudget (10 s) the realized span reaches about 100 s (foreground shape) or 130 s (background) against a SCHEDULED 30 s spread, and it lands twice — once in a realized gap and once in the duration-shaped circle-count estimator PUB-COALESCE records. So this entry is a promise about the SCHEDULE at every reachable roster, and must not be read as 'a peer's marker never expires': on iOS with background sharing on it CAN expire before the replacement lands, from FOUR circles up, which is an ordinary roster and not a corner. All three are stated on haven/lib/src/constants/location.dart, and their PROOF status differs, which is the reason to state it: only the Android 248 s is pinned, by equality per API regime (haven/test/services/background_fix_request_test.dart, 'a cold TTFF outruns the lead, and on API ≤ 30 it outruns the retention as well — the residual, exactly'). The iOS 235/238 s crossing and the 100/130 s serial span are arithmetic over kBurstConnectBudget, kBurstBacklogBudget, kBurstWindowBudget, kBurstPublishBudget and the stagger that NO test asserts — burstBound pins the composition of those budgets, never the seconds they add up to — so those two are DISCLOSED and not enforced, and moving a budget moves them silently. THE ROTATION FACTS THAT MAKE THE PERIOD ABSOLUTE ARE UNCHANGED and still worth stating, because they are what keeps a lost turn from compounding: _rotation outlives stopScheduling()/startScheduling() and outlives an emission reporting nothing eligible (circlesProvider degrades ANY roster-read failure to an empty list, so an empty emission is at least as often a transient FFI/keyring error as a real departure), so neither a backgrounding nor a failed roster read re-phases whose turn it is — pinned by 'a deferred circle is not deferred again by every resume', 'a transient empty roster emission does not re-phase whose turn it is' and 'a roster change keeps survivors' places in the queue', and structurally by scripts/ci/check_publish_rotation_fairness.sh, which pins _rotation.clear() to exactly ONE site inside build() and the survivor merge to below the _circles.isEmpty guard. What DOES rewind the queue is build() — a fresh container, or the invalidate in IdentityNotifier.deleteIdentity — and a process restart, which does not persist it; and because the roster keeps filterPublishEligibleCircles order (getVisibleCircles() orders by updated_at DESC) a rewind returns to the SAME head and re-serves the same first slice, a deterministic re-service and not a re-phase. At a bounded roster the first slice IS the roster, so a rewind serves all of it.

invariants.title: The routing tag is a pseudonym, and Haven never rotates it
invariants.statement: Published events carry nostr_group_id in the h tag and the real MLS group ID appears nowhere in the event JSON or any tag; Haven never rotates the tag itself — it never invokes the rotation the nostr-routing component permits — so a relay can group one circle's traffic for as long as no other client's admin rotates it. A rotation another client's admin makes is followed, and for the day both ids stand a relay that carries both can link them; after that day a history range a refused event owes still asks every id the circle keeps of each relay it was used with, so such a relay can link them again whenever a range is walked, until a routing change made more than the retained window later prunes the prior id. Publishing the raw MLS group ID, or leaving the copy attributing the stability to the protocol rather than to Haven, falsifies this.

event_kinds.note: h tag carries nostr_group_id.
The welcome gift wrap must also not leak the raw MLS group ID.

invariants.residual: Component presence is the invariant, NOT engine behaviour. cgka-engine's transport_group_id_of_group falls back to the RAW MLS GroupId when a group carries no NostrRoutingV1 (0x8004) component, and that value is what the peeler hex-encodes into the h tag — a direct Security Rule 4 violation with no engine-side refusal. Haven is safe today for two incidental reasons, neither tested: create_circle always mints the component, and accept_invitation fails closed if a joined group lacks routing. Residual path: an admin co-member clearing the component via UpdateAppComponents on an existing circle. The location seal (`seal_location_staging`) reads circle.nostr_group_id from STORAGE for publish targeting while the h tag comes from the ENGINE at wrap time, and nothing cross-checks the two. The cited test exercises only a Haven-created group with an intact component, so it cannot see this.

invariants.title: Invitations travel as unsigned rumors inside gift wraps with fresh authors
invariants.statement: The kind-444 Welcome rumor carries no signature (so a recipient cannot republish it as the inviter), it is delivered inside a NIP-59 kind-1059 gift wrap authored by a freshly generated key, and neither the wrap nor its tags leak the MLS group ID, the circle name or the roster; signing the rumor, reusing a wrap author, or adding any tag beyond p falsifies this.

peeler.rs builds the wrap with empty extra tags, so the only tag is p (recipient).

The READ side (nostr/giftwrap.rs:93) — the named nostr variant, which carries no number a numeric scan could find.

invariants.title: The expiry a circle's details sheet shows is the expiry this device stamps on its own location messages
invariants.statement: The circle-details subtitle reports the EFFECTIVE relay-retention window for the location messages THIS device sends into that circle — bounded_retention_secs applied to the group's declared 0x8005 component — and never the raw declaration. The two diverge in exactly the cases that matter: a circle that declares nothing, and one that declares longer than Haven's own window, both collapse to LOCATION_MESSAGE_RETENTION_SECS, while a SHORTER foreign declaration is honoured and is therefore shown as declared. A circle with no live MLS group shows no window at all rather than falling back to Haven's, because the fallback would report 'about four minutes' for a circle that cannot send. The copy states whose messages the number governs ('the location updates you send') and keeps the window a request to relays rather than a promise of deletion.

invariants.title: The inbox and KeyPackage relay lists are published under the identity key
invariants.statement: Haven publishes a kind-10050 inbox relay list and a kind-10002 NIP-65 list, both signed by the identity key and both fanned out to the relays already on them, and it publishes kind-30443 KeyPackages to those relays; consequently every URL a user adds to those lists becomes public and permanently linked to their pubkey, and the retired kind-10051 is not emitted at all. Gift wraps (kind 1059) are read only from the inbox list `inboxRelaysProvider` gives — the stored list kind 10050 is built from, or the compile-time seed while seeding has failed — by the invitation poller, the manual inbox refresh and the live-sync engine's inbox REQ, whose start is handed that list, over 96 h (the poller and the refresh from the wall clock; the engine from its inbox cursor, and 7 days on the one REQ made before any cursor exists); an empty list polls nothing rather than ask other relays for this pubkey's gift wraps.

invariants.title: No wire kind exists for the profile relay category
invariants.statement: RelayType::Profile::to_kind() returns None, so there is no kind an EventBuilder could be handed for a profile relay list and no code path can serialize that list into a published event; a relay that only carries location or invitation traffic therefore has no signed pointer telling it which relays the device uses for its profile. Adding a kind mapping, or publishing a kind-10002 that names the profile pool, falsifies this.

invariants.title: Haven operates no server of its own on any plane
invariants.statement: There is no Haven-operated relay, no Haven backend, and no account record: the seeded relays are third-party Nostr relays, identity creation takes no email, phone number or password, and the map plane's only first-party artefact is a single shared Stadia API key carrying no per-user identifier. Introducing a Haven-hosted endpoint that receives user data falsifies this.

invariants.title: No push notification plane exists
invariants.statement: No FCM/APNs/OneSignal-class dependency is declared in pubspec.yaml, and nothing under haven/ios registers for remote notifications (no remote-notification background mode, no aps-environment entitlement, no registerForRemoteNotifications), so no coordinator ever learns when someone in a circle has something to deliver.

invariants.title: No analytics, crash-reporting or advertising code ships
invariants.statement: The app declares no analytics, crash-reporting or ad SDK and contains no code path that reports usage, exceptions or identifiers to any third party; adding a Sentry/Crashlytics/Firebase-Analytics-class dependency, or a hand-rolled event-reporting HTTP call, falsifies this.
invariants.note: Backed by check 9b of that guard — the analytics/crash-reporting/advertising dependency surface, the sibling of check 9's push ban. Refuses such a dependency in every position that reaches a build (pubspec direct AND dev, the transitive pubspec.lock, both Cargo manifests and lockfiles, every haven/android build file, AndroidManifest components, Info.plist keys, PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy, a Podfile when present, and marker config files whose presence alone is an SDK). It cannot see a hand-rolled http.post of usage data, an SDK vendored inside another plugin's native artifact, or a Gradle coordinate assembled from variables.

invariants.title: More than one relay is seeded, and a new circle gets three, so no single relay can cut a user off
invariants.statement: PRODUCTION_DEFAULT_RELAYS holds exactly three wss:// relays run by independent operators, and no relay in that set is Haven-operated or individually required; shrinking the set to one — or to two, which is thinner than the copy discloses — falsifies the "several relays, so no single one can cut you off" promise. A circle Haven creates without named relays gets min(3, n) distinct relays from the eight-entry location pool (PRODUCTION_LOCATION_RELAYS, one registrable domain per entry): three, unless the user's own identity lists or a non-public host leave fewer than three entries eligible (INV-R-CIRCLE-RELAYS-FROM-LOCATION-POOL).

invariants.title: A new circle's relays are drawn at random from Haven's location pool, never from anyone's inbox
invariants.statement: A create the caller names no relays for (every create the app's UI makes: NostrCircleService.createCircle hands the driver the relays its own caller named, or none, and never the invitees' inbox relays, which serve only to deliver their Welcomes) takes min(3, n) distinct relays, drawn with OsRng (pick_location_relays, the one OsRng use in circle/location_pool.rs, over the pure pick_circle_relays), from PRODUCTION_LOCATION_RELAYS or, in a debug build, the list set_location_relays_for_test installed — n being the entries left once each is normalised, de-duplicated by authority (lower-cased host and port), kept only if foreign_relay_dialable admits it and passed through the hard tier. HARD exclusion: no relay whose authority appears in the user's Inbox, KeyPackage or Profile lists, the curated profile pool, the discovery plane or a contamination-ledger row recorded as an inbox, key-package or discovery relay, or a relay retired from the profile pool (CircleStorage::identity_relay_authorities, whose read errors fail the create) is ever picked, however it is spelled; a Welcome ledger row is not in the tier, because that relay took only an ephemeral-key gift wrap p-tagged to an invitee; when no entry is left the create is refused with the fieldless CircleError::NoLocationRelay (RefusalFfi::NoLocationRelay, shown as fixed copy) and nothing is persisted. SOFT exclusion: an entry one of the invitees lists as an inbox relay or a NIP-65 read or write relay is taken only to fill up to min(3, n) when too few others are left, so a crafted invitee list can neither steer the circle onto one relay nor block the create, and the fill never reaches past the hard tier. The pick never falls back to the full pool, to the inbox union or to the account seed. A caller that names relays gets them verbatim, never merged with the invitees' (the harnesses do this). The picked relays are the circle's routing component, sorted, and are recorded in the contamination ledger as CircleRouting before any Welcome is sent. No picked relay reaches a log line. check_profile_privacy_boundaries.sh holds the file to a CSPRNG (9b), the named tests to existence (11), the override out of library tests (12b) and every pool entry to a dated vetting row (14b). This becomes false if a create with no relays named takes the invitees' inbox relays, the user's own lists or the seed, if the draw stops being OsRng-backed, or if the hard tier is relaxed.

invariants.title: The location pool is Haven's own list, so its hostnames mark Haven users and probable co-members
invariants.statement: PRODUCTION_LOCATION_RELAYS is a list only Haven uses, and every member of a circle Haven creates without named relays dials the same three of its eight relays. A DNS or TLS SNI observer (an ISP, a Wi-Fi operator) can infer from those hostnames that a device runs Haven and that devices dialling the same three are probably in one circle; the pool's operators, together, can enumerate Haven users' IP addresses. Nothing in Haven mitigates either beyond the recorded absence of network-level unlinkability (P6).

invariants.title: The live-sync engine never authenticates and never fans out beyond the configured relays
invariants.statement: The engine Client is built with automatic_authentication(false) and no gossip, so it refuses every NIP-42 AUTH challenge (never signing a kind-22242 that would join the identity key to the circle traffic on that socket) and its relay pool equals exactly the configured circle-union-inbox set even after a kind-10002 advertises a phantom relay. verify_subscriptions must also stay off, or fresh REQs silently drop their first stored events.

event_kinds.note: Read-side: a kind-10002 advertising a phantom relay must not expand the engine's pool.

NIP-42 AUTH. Haven never signs one — build_engine_client sets automatic_authentication(false). Declared so the kind-based closed world can see the one kind whose appearance would falsify this invariant.

invariants.title: The publish relay pool sends no keepalives and closes between bursts
invariants.statement: Every RelayManager publish pool — the UI isolate's, the Android foreground service's, any other isolate's that builds one, and the live session's own drive pool, which the bridge builds with the session, which carries nothing but the fanout driver's calls, and which the session closes whenever it cuts its radio — registers each relay through RelayPool::add_relay with publish_relay_options(): ping(false), so no WebSocket keepalive frame leaves the device between publish bursts; sleep_when_idle(true) with a 10 s idle timeout, so the socket closes within roughly a minute of the last publish rather than being held open; and reconnect(false), because the idle monitor runs only inside a live connection task, so a dropped socket that kept reconnecting would never reach Sleeping. Client::add_relay must never be used on that pool: for a URL the pool already holds it ORs RelayServiceFlags::default() (READ | WRITE | PING) onto the live relay and silently restores the keepalive on every socket. Every RelayManager fetch primitive leaves no subscription registered behind it, so nothing holds the socket awake after a fetch. The durable fanout publishes on this same pool through MDK's relay client (transport-nostr-adapter NostrSdkRelayClient, built over the pool's own client by RelayManager::fanout_transport), which takes no relay options and would add a target it does not know write-only with the SDK's defaults: FanoutTransport::publish registers the target itself first, through the same RelayPool::add_relay with publish_relay_options(), so MDK's client finds it already held and leaves it as registered, and after the call takes the keepalive back off the target if it is set — MDK's client adds, through the SDK, a target that was absent at its own check and present at its add, which ORs PING onto the relay the pool holds; the publish dials that target and no other relay the pool holds, and the wedged-socket check runs after it; a target that fails Haven's relay policy on its parsed URL is never registered or dialled. The pool's relays carry the READ flag, because the same client runs Haven's targeted fetches and the pool silently skips a relay without it, so a pool-wide subscription would be sent to every relay Haven publishes to: none is ever opened on this pool, and the subscription half of MDK's relay client and of its adapter (activate_account, NostrRelayClient::subscribe, the notification forwarder, MDK's NIP-77 reconciler) is never called. Haven's own NIP-77 session runs on this pool inside a wake, one relay at a time, as a dry run with an empty local set, and registers no subscription (RelayManager::neg_remote_ids, check 5 of check_publish_client_no_subscription.sh). The publish client holds no signer and is built with automatic_authentication(false), so it never answers a relay's NIP-42 challenge: an answer would be the identity key's signature over a relay's challenge on a socket that carries a circle's routing id. One MDK relay client is built per RelayManager, and every path that registers a relay on this pool — the publish ladders, the fire-and-forget publish, the per-relay fetch and the fanout publish — finds one the pool already holds under the pool's read lock and does not register it again, so none of them queues a writer behind a send that is waiting for its OK. The ENGINE pool (build_engine_client) deliberately KEEPS the pool's ping, because it holds standing REQs and carries no other traffic: turning it off there re-creates the dead-but-running relay blackout that nothing notices until the 15-minute health tick.

invariants.title: A NIP-77 reconciliation tells a relay its filter and nothing the device holds
invariants.statement: A NIP-77 session tells a relay the filter alone — kind 445, one circle's #h, since (the clock-only until less 30 days, never the device's own inventory floor), until and limit — and no id or fingerprint of what the device holds: its local set is empty, so its opening message is the empty set (6100000200) and every later client message an empty IdList or a Skip, and as a dry run in the download direction it sends no EVENT. It follows up only with a by-id REQ, carrying the same #h, to that same relay, for ids that relay reported and the device's own record for that circle lacks — never consulting what another circle processed — and that request names those ids, which tells that relay the device holds the rest of what it reported in the window. It runs only inside a background burst, once at a live foreground entry and inside a catch-up sweep, at most four routes per ten seconds and never on a timer of its own; a relay that refuses NIP-77 is asked once for each route of the first pass that meets it — the routes of a pass run concurrently, so each asks before any refusal is recorded — and never again in that process; its subscription id is fresh per session; and every session of a burst ends by NEG-CLOSE, NEG-ERR or its socket's close before the pause returns. MDK's reconcile_subscription, which would advertise the device's inventory to the relay, is never called.

invariants.title: Every frame Haven sends a relay reaches only a relay whose plane admits it
invariants.statement: Every client-to-relay frame Haven sends reaches only a relay whose plane admits that verb, kind and exact tag or filter-key set for that binding, as the allow matrix ROWS (tooling/e2e/local-relay/src/planes/policy.rs, rendered verbatim in haven-core/SECURITY.md "The relay-plane allow matrix") states it: a circle's kind 445 on that circle's routing (a commit on the targets frozen when it was staged, the routing a relay change leaves included), its #h REQs and NIP-77 sessions where that routing stands and its by-id fetches where it is kept; a Welcome on its invitee's inbox list; the account's own key package and relay lists on its own lists, each list naming no relay of another plane; kind 0 and its lookups on the profile plane alone; another account's relay lists and key packages asked of the discovery plane or of that account's own lists; and a CLOSE only for a subscription that relay was sent, and a NEG-MSG or NEG-CLOSE only for a session its own connection opened. One judge (judge) applies it to every frame in-process relays recorded across a circle's lifecycle — three real engines over thirteen relays, one per role, through the live plane, both catch-up planes, invites, a relay change, a leave and the profile plane — and to the FFI's key-package, relay-list and profile orchestration with the sender known; in the lifecycle run every relay any client dials is a relay of the test's world, and in both runs a crossing planted on a plane is reported exactly. The soak rig's O7 applies the same judge to every frame every device of a soak world sent — with the sender known on a device's own and alias endpoints — after every arm and the nemesis phase, its profile and key-package planes driven under a downed profile relay (S26), and its own planted crossings each reported.
invariants.residual: Two things this does not hold. (a) An invitee's own relay lists steer an invite onto other planes: the lifecycle run's last phase pins, as current behaviour, the key-package lookup asked of a profile relay that the invitee's NIP-65 write set names and the Welcome sent to a location relay that the invitee's inbox list names first (PLAN_v2 section 4 finding 1, owner decision OQ-1: no product change in this work); that expected set becomes empty when a rule drops such entries. (b) The lifecycle run judges with no sender, so a request bound to another identity's own list there (an inbox REQ by #p of an account other than the sending device's) passes; the per-identity bindings are proved only by the FFI run, with the sender known. The dial check is the lifecycle run's alone: the FFI run arms no dial witness, its binary's tests sharing one process concurrently. O7 judges a frame on a plane's canonical endpoint (catch-up sweeps, the rig's inbox reads, an invite's key-package lookup) with no sender, so there too a request bound to another identity's own list passes. O7 holds a location on a relay a change left admissible (a member that has not applied the change still seals for the routing it holds, and the rig knows that instant for the stager alone), and grades no discovery traffic: a soak process points discovery at a port that refuses every dial.

invariants.title: On the hermetic core-flow lanes, every frame Haven puts on the wire lands on a relay whose role admits it
invariants.statement: On the recorded core-flow lanes (Android and iOS, poll and live-sync), every client-to-relay EVENT, REQ filter and NEG-OPEN filter outside the harness, at or below the sentinel, reaches only a proxy listen whose declared role (inbox, key-package, discovery, location; no profile listen exists there) admits its verb, kind and shape: a kind-445 and every #h REQ and NEG-OPEN only on a relay of its circle's declared routing, a kind-1059 only on an inbox relay some kind-10050 of its recipient names, a kind-30443 or kind-10002 only on a relay its author's kind-10002 names, a kind-10050 only on its own inbox relays, a key-package or relay-list lookup only on discovery or on the target's own lists, nothing at all on discovery, and no kind 0 or kind-0 REQ anywhere, since that lane's profile plane fails closed. Every declared role is witnessed, every circle with traffic is declared, and every frame's listen is declared, so a run that judged nothing is a failure rather than a pass. False if any such frame reaches a listen outside its role.
invariants.residual: ROLE PLACEMENT, not the per-identity bindings: the oracle judges every frame with no sender, so a request on another identity's own list passes it; those bindings are held by INV-R-RELAY-PLANE-CONTAINMENT's L1b test and the soak oracle O7. The lanes give one listen three roles — the account's inbox and key-package relay, which discovery also reads through the default-relay fallback, the same seed-and-discovery overlap production has — so a frame for one of those roles on the relay of another of them is not told apart here; the Rust layers, where each role has its own relay, tell them apart. A circle's routing is the one the drive declares from Rust's view of the circle (CircleFfi.relays), so a routing Rust itself recorded wrong is not caught here. Blossom (HTTP) is outside every relay oracle. The unproxied multi-relay lanes (relay customization, the profile plane, key-package rotation) carry no recorder: their relays are judged from the STORE, which shows no REQ, no NEG session, no expired location and no binding beyond the kind.
